A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Style Matching Score (SMS) research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original stylization experiments, quantitative comparisons, a user study, ablations, runtime measurements, and supplementary qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–5, and revises several qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The style-matching objective, progressive spectrum regularization, semantic-aware gradient refinement, timestep sampling, and feed-forward training procedure are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is relocated without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions retain PIE, LHQ, DIV2K, the spectrum-analysis datasets, and the same stylization tasks and artistic-style coverage. Replaced qualitative examples remain within already represented domains and styles.

E2.justification: The single-image comparisons retain FreeStyle, StyleID, InstantStyle-Plus, Style-LoRA, and DDS. Feed-forward comparisons retain Scenimefy, DDS, and PDS; Appendix D already includes SDS and the style-LoRA variants in v1.

E3.justification: The stated model, training settings, datasets and splits, metrics, and user-study design are unchanged. Figure 11 uses the same six loss weights from 0.00001 to 0.005; reversing their display order does not change the sensitivity-test protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 revises the loss-weight sensitivity evidence: Figure 11 replaces the indoor-scene sweep with a horse example identified as kids illustration. The other sensitivity rows, component ablations, spectrum analysis, and identity-loss comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same aggregate-score reporting. Neither reports additional seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. Qualitative results change in Figure 11's replacement sensitivity example and Figure 19, where spider and bee sketch examples are replaced by a grain field and blueberries.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and definitions in the main text and the KL-gradient and score-function derivation in Appendix B are retained. No new assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical corrections appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about distribution-based stylization, balancing style and content, and application to lightweight feed-forward generators. The added abstract background sentence does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of comparative performance and component behavior remain unchanged. Appendix E.2 restates the existing loss-weight tradeoff, while Appendix H retains the same limitations concerning insufficient LoRA content diversity and reduced stylization when preservation is strengthened.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit code-repository link in the abstract and appendix, providing access information absent from v1. The implementation settings, LoRA-source information, pseudocode, and runtime disclosures otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds an introduction citation to OmniConsistency. It also formalizes the already-linked Civitai resource as a bibliography entry; the substantive positioning relative to previous stylization and score-distillation methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds an abstract background sentence, acknowledgments, and a corresponding-author footnote, reorders affiliation numbering, and lightly rewrites the loss-weight discussion. The main section organization and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 corrects Figure 7's panel lettering, reverses Figure 11's weight columns and clarifies its style labels, and replaces panels in Figures 11 and 19. It also relocates appendix floats and enlarges Figures 14–15 without substantially redesigning the document.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves usability through explicit code-access information, corrected Figure 7 labels, and clearer style identification in Figure 11. The revised sensitivity example provides limited additional qualitative support, while the unchanged method, theory, and numerical validation keep the overall improvement modest.
